coverage.note: The OpenGov contract story named no street address. The drug-free housing story named two, both recorded below and both declined.

findings.description: Recorded so the hit is not read again. A story on two drug-free housing bills describes this as the city's only drug-free permanent supportive housing site, with 42 units, and notes it offers no programming aimed at substance-use disorder.

citation.label: Mission Local, “Both California and San Francisco passed drug-free housing bills. How would they coexist?,” 3 September 2026

raw.text: There is currently only one permanent supportive housing site with 42 units at 1174 Folsom St. that is drug-free

publish.note: The entry is the headline, and this headline is about two bills and how they would interact — it says nothing about this building, and in ten years a page carrying it would be carrying a question about pending legislation. The building is named here as an illustration of a policy point, which is the passing mention news/AGENTS.md declines. That it is the city's only drug-free supportive housing site is a fact about a program's footprint, and one that a signature or a budget could make untrue within the year.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 1174 FOLSOM ST → parcel 3730409; sf-parcels has blklot 3730409 active, 1174–1174 FOLSOM; the 2025 roll records it as commercial retail. EAS files the address under parcel 3730023, which sf-parcels reports retired; the active parcel its coordinates fall in is 3730409.
resolution.note: No page at this path yet; the parcel is the publisher's to seed.

findings.description: Recorded so the hit is not read again. The same story describes this as a permanent supportive housing site in South of Market for transitional-aged youth, currently housing 22 formerly homeless people aged 18 to 24, managed by the non-profit Five Keys, with case managers on site. It is also the building photographed for the story's lead graphic.

citation.label: Mission Local, “Both California and San Francisco passed drug-free housing bills. How would they coexist?,” 3 September 2026
citation.locator: lead graphic caption and mid-article section

raw.text: Staff and tenants at a transitional-aged youth site at 42 Otis St. say the on-site programming is paramount.

publish.note: Declined for the same reason as 1174 Folsom, and more firmly. The building is the backdrop of the story's photograph — the exact example news/AGENTS.md gives of a mention that gives a page nothing — and the passage about it is a profile of the residents: a named tenant, her age, her disability, her housing history. Nothing in that may reach a page, and what is left once it is removed is a headline about legislation. Neither the count of residents nor their ages is recorded above.

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses has 42 OTIS ST but it does not join to one parcel. 42 OTIS ST's coordinates fall in 20 active parcels (3505080, 3505055, 3505075, 3505076…), which is what a condominium looks like in sf-parcels: one parcel per unit, none of them the building.
resolution.note: The address is a condominium today, and the directory contract in the root AGENTS.md defers those: each unit has its own parcel and none of them is the building the record names.
